title: Owners of San Francisco homes, and how their other homes fare
question: Do the companies that own or run San Francisco nursing homes also own homes elsewhere with heavy federal fines, abuse markers or special-focus status?
finding: The federal ownership file names 24 organizations as owners or managers of San Francisco homes; 15 of them also hold other homes. None has at least three other homes and fines per home at least twice the national average of $30,351. Highest fines per other home: Providence Administrative Consulting Services Inc (Victorian Post Acute): 70 other homes in 12 states, $3.6 million of fines, 49 immediate-jeopardy citations, 5 on special focus; Providence Group Inc (Central Gardens Post Acute, City View Post Acute): 31 other homes in 9 states, $1.3 million of fines, 21 immediate-jeopardy citations, 1 on special focus; Providence Group North LLC (San Francisco Post Acute): 11 other homes in 1 states, $330,358 of fines, 2 immediate-jeopardy citations, 0 on special focus.
how: From the federal ownership file (organizations only; people are never matched), every role listed (direct and indirect owners, operational or managerial control, mortgage holders and the like). The organization's name, without punctuation and endings such as LLC, is matched across the whole country; then fines, abuse markers, special-focus status and immediate-jeopardy citations of its other homes are added up from the provider and citation files.
limits: A name match across states can join two unrelated companies with the same name, and holding companies and lenders appear on many homes they do not run day to day. Fines depend on the State's inspectors as much as on the homes. A chain's worst homes say nothing by themselves about its San Francisco home.
